scenes.heading: What verbal reasoning tests
scenes.sub: Thinking with words, against the clock
scenes.say: Verbal reasoning isn't about knowing the longest words. It's about spotting patterns in words and following clues carefully. Let's see what the section looks like and how to pace yourself.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A locksmith picks the right tool for each lock
scenes.science: You name the question type, then use its trick
scenes.breaks: A locksmith can take as long as needed. You have about 45 seconds a question, so pick fast.
scenes.say: A locksmith doesn't use the same tool on every lock. First they look at the lock, then they pick the right tool. Do the same: name the question type, then use its trick. The difference is time. You have about forty-five seconds a question.

scenes.heading: Six question types
scenes.say: You'll meet six types: analogies, odd one out, synonyms and antonyms, letter series and codes, hidden words, and logical deduction. Each one has its own trick, and we'll learn them one by one.

scenes.heading: Your pace
scenes.question: 40 questions in 30 minutes. How long for each question?
scenes.say: Our practice tests have forty questions in thirty minutes. Thirty minutes is one thousand eight hundred seconds. Divide by forty and you get forty-five seconds each. Easy questions take less, so you save time for hard ones.

scenes.heading: Use this on every question
steps: Test it on all four options
Pick the best and move on
scenes.say: Here's the routine. Name the question type. Find the rule before you look at the options. Test the rule on all four options. Then pick the best one and move on.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Bird is to nest as dog is to ___ . bark, kennel, puppy, bone
lines: Rule: a nest is a bird's home
scenes.say: Bird is to nest as dog is to what? The rule: a nest is a bird's home. Bark is a sound, a puppy is a young dog, a bone is food. Only kennel is a home. Every option was linked to dog, but only one follows the rule.

scenes.heading: Stuck on a question?

right.title: Do
points: Come back if time is left

scenes.say: Stuck? Don't sink three minutes into one question, and don't leave it blank. Cross out what you know is wrong, take your best guess, flag it and move on. Check the instructions about guessing on the day.

Quick recap. There are six question types. Work at about forty-five seconds each. Find the rule first, test it on all four options, and if you're stuck, flag it, guess and move on. Now try the practice questions!
